segments.text: [README.md] # Knowledge Acquisition Studio
[README.md] ## Purpose Ingest tutorials, transcripts and learning sources, extract actionable knowledge, verify it, and apply it to projects.
[README.md] ## Expected outputs - source map - timestamped notes - knowledge base - step-by-step procedure - verification evidence - original educational content

[README.md] ## Autonomous execution The project follows: **Task -> Execute -> Verify -> Fix/Retry -> Complete -> Update Status -> Next Unblocked Task** See `docs/director/director-section.md` and `workflows/knowledge-acquisition-studio-workflow.md`.
[tests/README.md] # Tests Add unit, integration and end-to-end fixtures here.

[docs/architecture/architecture.md] # Architecture — Knowledge Acquisition Studio ```text User Goal | v Orchestrator | +--> Input / Validation +--> Specialist Agents +--> Research / Knowledge (when required) +--> Artifact Generation +--> QA / Verification | +--> PASS --> Status --> Next Task | +--> FAIL --> Diagnose --> Retry ``` The architecture is intentionally modular so individual agents can be replaced without redesigning the whole workflow.

[docs/operations/cookies.md] # Operations — Reels cookies Reels are served to logged-in sessions. Without a session, Instagram returns `empty media response`. This document records the tested options on this host (2026-11-02, `yt-dlp 2026.10.26`).

[docs/operations/cookies.md] ## Test results | Browser | Cookies found (instagram) | Extraction result | |---|---|---| | Firefox (`kvl29ev8.default-release`) | **0** | 342 cookies extracted, 0 undecryptable | | Brave (`Default`) | 9 | 126 extracted, **366 undecryptable** (keyring locked over SSH) | | Vivaldi (`Default`) | 7 | **0 extracted**, 9 undecryptable | Interpretation: - **Firefox is the only browser that decrypts cleanly** on this host, but it has no Instagram session yet. One login there is all that's needed. - Brave holds the Instagram session but its cookie encryption depends on the desktop keyring, which is un...

[docs/operations/cookies.md] ## Recommended path 1. Open Firefox on the machine and log into Instagram once (remember-me). 2. Keep using `--cookies-from-browser firefox` — no credential file is ever written. ```bash yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser firefox --simulate --print "%(title)s" "<reel-url>" ```

[docs/operations/cookies.md] ## Fallback path (exported cookies) Only if Firefox is unavailable: 1. Export Netscape-format `cookies.txt` from a logged-in browser. 2. Save as `~/.hermes/cookies/instagram.txt`, `chmod 600`. 3. Reference the **path** in config; never copy it into the repository or artifacts. ```yaml sources: reels: cookies_from_browser: firefox # preferred cookies_file: /home/hardik/.hermes/cookies/instagram.txt # fallback ```

[docs/operations/cookies.md] ## Expiry and failure behaviour - Auth failure is detected as `empty media response` / `login required`, **not** as a network error. - On detection the source is marked `quarantined` with reason `auth_expired`; the daemon does not retry it (retrying burns quota and can trip rate limits). - Quarantine is visible in `status.json` and in the daily run report.

[docs/operations/cookies.md] ## Security notes - `~/.hermes` is `700`, `.env` is `600` (verified 2026-11-02). - Cookies grant account access: treat `cookies.txt` as a password. Never commit, never include in `derived/`, never log the value (log only "cookies loaded: N"). - `--cookies-from-browser` copies the cookie DB to a temp file; it must be cleaned up by the tool. Do not point `--cookies` at the live browser database.

[docs/operations/operations.md] ## Runtime principles - Prefer local/open-source tools where practical. - Keep configuration outside code. - Persist task state. - Preserve logs and evidence. - Make failures recoverable.
[docs/operations/operations.md] ## Operational status The status agent should report the current phase, completed work, blockers, risks and next task.
[docs/director/director-section.md] # Director's Section — Knowledge Acquisition Studio
[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Intent Ingest tutorials, transcripts and learning sources, extract actionable knowledge, verify it, and apply it to projects.

[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Non-negotiables - Follow the approved project requirements. - Preserve source/provenance where applicable. - Do not silently invent missing inputs. - Do not mark work complete without verification. - Prefer free/open-source/local solutions where practical.

[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Continuity rules - Maintain consistent project state. - Do not contradict approved decisions without recording a new decision. - Preserve naming and artifact contracts.
[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Quality bar The output must be usable, testable, reproducible and clearly documented.

[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Prohibited deviations - Skipping QA to claim completion. - Hiding failed tasks. - Changing core requirements without a recorded decision. - Replacing evidence with assumptions.
[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Approval criteria A release is approved only when all required acceptance tests pass and status is updated.

[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Phase gates (v2.0) Phase transitions are exit tests, not opinions (`docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md` §4): | Gate | Exit condition | |---|---| | 0 → 1 | Requirements v2.0 and acceptance criteria exist; blocking open questions answered or waived. | | 1 → 2 | Manifest, config and status layers implemented; AC-01, AC-14, AC-19 pass. | | 2 → 3 | Ingest, transcript and notes pipeline; AC-03…AC-06, AC-18 pass. | | 3 → 4 | Knowledge, procedures, source map, retry, idempotency; AC-07…AC-13, AC-15…AC-17 pass. | | 4 → 5 | QA report, application, derived content, Skill packaging; AC-20…AC-23 pass. ...

[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Assumption policy (v2.0) When an input is missing, the agent must do exactly one of: 1. Ask the Director and record the answer in `docs/requirements/open-questions.md`, or 2. Apply the documented default **only if** the Director explicitly waives the question, and record the waiver. An unrecorded assumption is a defect, not a shortcut.

[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Freeze policy (v2.0) Requirements are frozen at v2.0. Any behavioural change requires an ADR in `docs/decisions/`, a version bump in `docs/requirements/requirements.md`, and a matching `skills/knowledge-acquisition-studio/VERSION`.
[docs/director/director-section.md] ## Sign-off Phase 0 is signed off when the Director resolves or waives OQ-1, OQ-2, OQ-3, OQ-4 and OQ-7.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] # Acceptance Criteria — Knowledge Acquisition Studio - **Version:** 1.0 (Phase 0 freeze) - **Frozen on:** 2026-11-02 - **Applies to:** requirements v2.1 - **Gate rule:** a criterion is *passed* only when the stated evidence exists and is reproducible.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ## 1. Conventions - `PASS` requires a command, fixture or artifact path that a second person can re-run. - Every criterion is verified by the **verification agent** and recorded as `evidence/<task_id>.json`. - Evidence record shape: ```json { "task_id": "t-0007", "criteria": ["AC-03"], "result": "pass", "artifacts": ["sources/src-1a2b3c4d5e6f/source.json"], "command": "pytest tests/test_ingest.py -k checksum", "run_at": "2026-11-02T18:40:00Z", "notes": null } ``` - Manual review is allowed only for AC marked `review`; everything else must be automated.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-01 — Manifest validation (FR-01) · automated Given a manifest missing a required field or containing an unknown field When the orchestrator starts Then it exits non-zero, prints the field path and the expected type, and writes no files under `sources/`, `notes/`, `knowledge/` or `evidence/`.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-02 — Unsupported source kind (FR-02) · automated Given a manifest declaring `kind: epub` and no registered epub adapter When ingestion runs Then the task is marked `failed`, the reason names the unsupported kind, and remaining sources still ingest.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-03 — Source Record completeness (FR-02) · automated Given a successfully ingested source When `sources/<source_id>/source.json` is read Then all fields in requirements §4 are present, `checksum` equals the sha256 recomputed from `raw/`, and `source_id` equals `src-<checksum[0:12]>`.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-04 — Raw immutability (FR-03) · automated Given a source already ingested When ingestion runs again with identical bytes Then the raw file hash and mtime are unchanged and no duplicate record is created. When ingestion runs with different bytes under the same `source_id` Then it fails with a checksum-conflict error and does not overwrite `raw/`.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-05 — Transcript normalization (FR-04) · automated Given a completed transcription When `transcript.json` is read Then segments are ordered, `start < end`, `start[n] >= end[n-1]` (no overlap), no segment exceeds 30 s, and every segment has non-empty `text`.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-06 — Note provenance (FR-05) · automated Given generated notes for a source When each note bullet is checked Then it carries `source_id` and a timestamp range that exists within a transcript segment of that source; any bullet failing this fails the criterion.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-07 — Knowledge unit integrity (FR-06) · automated Given `knowledge/units.json` When validated Then every unit has `id`, `statement`, `source_refs` (≥1), `confidence` ∈ {`low`,`medium`,`high`}, ids are unique and equal to `k-<sha256(statement)[0:12]>`.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-08 — Procedural executability (FR-07) · automated Given `knowledge/procedures/*.md` When parsed Then each procedure has an ordered list of numbered steps, every step references ≥1 knowledge unit id that exists, and no step is empty or a restatement of a section heading.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-09 — Source map coverage (FR-08) · automated Given N ingested sources When `knowledge/source-map.json` is read Then it contains exactly N entries, each `source_id` appears once, and no entry references a missing Source Record.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-10 — Verification gate (FR-09) · automated Given a task whose evidence artifact is absent or has `result: "fail"` When completion is attempted Then the task stays `in_progress`/`failed`, the orchestrator reports a gate violation, and `status.json` is not advanced.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-11 — Bounded retry and escalation (FR-10) · automated Given an agent that raises on every attempt and `max_retries: 3` When the task runs Then exactly 4 attempts are recorded (1 + 3), each with diagnostics, the task ends `failed` with `escalated: true`, and no further tasks from that branch run.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-12 — Idempotent re-run (FR-11) · automated Given a completed task When the same task is executed again with unchanged inputs Then artifact count is unchanged, file contents are byte-identical except `generated_at`, and `status.json` records no duplicate completions.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-13 — Deterministic ids (FR-11) · automated Given two independent runs over the same source set on different dates When unit and source ids are compared Then the id sets are identical.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-14 — Status contract (FR-12) · automated Given any completed or failed task When `status.json` and `docs/status/status.md` are read Then both contain current phase, completed items, evidence references, risks, remaining work, next executable task and an ISO-8601 timestamp; `status.md` matches `status.json`.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-15 — Provenance resolution (FR-13) · automated Given every artifact under `notes/`, `knowledge/`, `derived/` and `application/` When all `source_ids` are resolved Then every id maps to an existing `sources/<source_id>/source.json`; zero dangling references.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-16 — Offline operation (FR-14) · automated Given `network.enabled: false` and only local file sources When the full pipeline runs with the network interface disabled Then it completes and all Must criteria pass.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-17 — Network opt-in (FR-14) · automated Given `network.enabled: false` When any adapter or agent attempts an outbound connection Then the attempt is blocked, logged with the target, and the run fails loudly rather than degrading silently.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-18 — Path confinement (FR-15) · automated Given a manifest value containing `../` or an absolute path outside the project root When processed Then it is rejected before any write, and no file outside the root is created or modified.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-19 — Unknown key rejection (FR-16) · automated Given a manifest or config with an unknown key When loaded Then loading fails with the unknown key path; it does not warn-and-continue.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-20 — Application report (FR-17) · review Given a completed knowledge base When knowledge is applied to a downstream project Then `application/report.md` names the target project, lists the applied units with their ids, and states the observable change made.

[docs/testing/acceptance-criteria.md] ### AC-21 — Original content separation (FR-18) · review Given `derived/` content When reviewed Then quoted source material is clearly marked with source and timestamp, and original writing is distinguishable from quotes.

[docs/testing/test-plan.md] ## Required gates - Input validation - Agent contract validation - Artifact existence - Output schema validation - Error handling - Retry behavior - End-to-end execution - Reproducibility
[docs/testing/test-plan.md] ## Definition of done A task is complete only when its acceptance criteria have passed and evidence is recorded.

[docs/testing/test-plan.md] ## Acceptance criteria Behavioural gates are defined in `acceptance-criteria.md` (AC-01…AC-23), with Given/When/Then form, evidence shape and the phase-gate table. This plan covers the *mechanism*; the criteria cover the *assertions*.

[docs/implementation/phase3.md] ## Deliberate limits - **No vault projection or hand-edit detection** (AC-24, AC-25) — Phase 4. - **No daemon trigger** (ADR-006 D18) — Phase 4. - **No QA report, application report, derived content or Skill packaging** (AC-20…AC-23) — Phase 5. - **No local model fallback** (ADR-006 D20).

[docs/implementation/phase2.md] ## Provider findings (recorded, not silently worked around)

[docs/implementation/phase2.md] - LLM7 audio (`Voxtral-Small-24B-2507`) calls `/audio/transcriptions` but returns `402 insufficient_balance` on this account. The chain falls through to Groq Whisper, which is validated end to end. - LLM7 chat (`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`) is the validated extraction model. Its note JSON used an alternate key shape (`timestamp`/`note`); `extract._coerce_note` now accepts both, so a chatty model cannot break the pipeline. - Groq's Cloudflare layer rejects the default `Python-urllib` agent with HTTP 403 / error 1010. `http.USER_AGENT` identifies `kas/0.1` and is sent on every request. - Unorouter's...

[docs/implementation/phase2.md] ## Deliberate limits - **No knowledge units, procedures or source map.** Those are Phase 3 (AC-07, AC-08, AC-09). - **No retry/escalation or idempotency harness** beyond raw immutability (AC-10…AC-13) — Phase 3. - **No vault projection or hand-edit detection** (AC-24, AC-25) — Phase 4/5. - **No daemon trigger** (ADR-006 D18) — Phase 4. - **No local model fallback.** Provider exhaustion fails loudly with the provider's error body (ADR-006 D20).

Verification gate + bounded retry/escalation (AC-10, AC-11) and idempotent re-run harness (AC-12). 5. Provenance sweep across `notes/`, `knowledge/`, `derived/`, `application/` (AC-15). 6. Offline mode enforcement (`network.enabled: false`) (AC-16, AC-17).

[docs/implementation/phase1.md] ## Deliberate limits - **No pipeline.** `run` validates, prepares directories and writes status. It does not ingest, transcribe or extract. [docs/requirements/requirements.md] # Requirements — Knowledge Acquisition Studio - **Version:** 2.1 (Phase 0 freeze; ADR-006 applied) - **Status:** Frozen — conditional on the blocking questions in `docs/requirements/open-questions.md` - **Frozen on:** 2026-11-02 (rev 2.1: 2026-11-02) - **Owner:** Director - **Supersedes:** v1.0 (2026-09-06)

[docs/requirements/requirements.md] ## 1. Purpose Ingest tutorials, transcripts and learning sources, extract actionable knowledge, verify it, and apply it to projects. The system converts untrusted, unstructured learning material into **traceable, verifiable, reusable knowledge artifacts**.

[docs/requirements/requirements.md] ### 2.1 In scope - Ingest a declared set of sources described by a project manifest. - Preserve the original bytes and full provenance of every source. - Produce timestamped notes, a knowledge base, and step-by-step procedures. - Verify every produced artifact against a written acceptance criterion. - Apply extracted knowledge to a downstream project and record the application. - Persist status, decisions and evidence for every task. - Package the stable workflow as a versioned Skill.

[docs/requirements/requirements.md] ### 2.2 Out of scope (v0.x) - Publishing or redistributing ingested material. - Copyright circumvention, DRM removal, or scraping behind authentication without explicit consent recorded in the manifest. - Real-time / streaming ingestion. - Multi-user accounts, roles or hosted service. - Fine-tuning or training models on ingested content. - Automatic purchase or download of paid sources.

Actors | Actor | Responsibility | |---|---| | Director (human) | Approves scope, resolves open questions, signs off releases | | Orchestrator | Decomposes goal into tasks, selects next unblocked task, enforces gates | | Ingestion adapters | Normalize one source origin into a Source Record | | Specialist agents | Transcribe, research, extract, compose, apply | | Verification agent | Executes acceptance criteria, emits evidence | | Status agent | Persists status, decisions, risks, next task |

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] # ADR-005 — Model provider selection (LLM7 primary, Unorouter failover) - **Date:** 2026-11-02 - **Status:** Accepted - **Deciders:** Director - **Related:** OQ-3, requirements §5 FR-06/FR-09, acceptance-criteria AC-07/AC-23

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] OQ-3 asked which runtime performs extraction and verification. The Director chose LLM7 over OpenRouter, with Unorouter as an alternative. Both endpoints were probed from the host:

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] | Provider | Base URL | Auth | Models | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | LLM7 | `https://api.llm7.io/v1` | `LLM7_API_KEY` | 12+ | OpenAI-compatible; text and audio models | | Unorouter | `https://api.unorouter.com/v1` | `UNOROUTER_API_KEY` | **325** | OpenAI-compatible; many `:free`, plus `claude-*`/`gpt-*` |
[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] Verified LLM7 entries:

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] | Model | Input | Context | Price / 1M in·out | Tools | |---|---|---|---|---| | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` | text | 400 k | $0.02 · $0.04 | yes | | `GLM-5.3-Flash` | text | 400 k | $0.02 · $0.04 | yes | | `Inkling-Small` | text | 512 k | $0.50 · $1.20 | yes | | `Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507` | **audio** | — | — | yes | | `Voxtral-Small-24B-2507` | **audio** | — | — | yes |

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] **D11 — LLM7 is the primary provider.** - Extraction, notes and procedure generation: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`. - Verification: `GLM-5.3-Flash` — a different model family from the generator, so a pass is not the generator agreeing with itself. This directly strengthens AC-10. - Transcription: `Voxtral-Small-24B-2507` (audio → text), with Groq `whisper-large-v3` as fallback.

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] **D12 — Unorouter is failover, not primary.** Used when LLM7 returns errors/timeouts beyond the retry budget. Model id is pinned in `config/default.yaml`, never resolved dynamically at runtime.

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] **D13 — Every artifact records its producer.** `provider`, `model`, `base_url` and `request_id` go into artifact metadata and into `evidence/<task_id>.json`. A run with an unknown producer is invalid.

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] **D14 — Model ids are validated before a run.** The orchestrator checks the configured model id appears in the provider's `/v1/models` and aborts with a named error otherwise. Cheap check, prevents silent 404-to-fallback.
[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] **D15 — Secrets stay in `~/.hermes/.env`.** Config references environment variable names only (`api_key_env: LLM7_API_KEY`).

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] ## Consequences - Cost is negligible for the chosen models (~$0.02/1M in, $0.04/1M out). - Two model families means extraction and verification failures are less correlated. - LLM7 is a small provider: an outage blocks the pipeline unless Unorouter is configured. OQ-10 records whether a fully local fallback is required. - Voxtral removes the hard dependency on Groq for transcription, but its timestamp behaviour is unproven — AC-05 must be tested against it, and Groq Whisper must remain validated as the fallback path. - Unorouter's 325-model catalogue is a moving target; pinning ids (D12) keeps...

[docs/decisions/ADR-005-model-providers.md] ## Open items - OQ-10: behaviour when LLM7 **and** Unorouter both fail (fail loudly vs local model). - Confirm Voxtral emits segment timestamps; if it only returns plain text, word-level timing must come from Groq Whisper or an alignment pass (lyrical-video already uses forced alignment, which can be reused).

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] # ADR-006 — Output to Obsidian, publishable content, daemon trigger - **Date:** 2026-11-02 - **Status:** Accepted - **Deciders:** Director - **Resolves:** OQ-2, OQ-4, OQ-7, OQ-9, OQ-10 - **Related:** ADR-004 (artifact contract), ADR-005 (providers)

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] ## Context Phase 0 needed five answers before Phase 2 could start: where output goes, what the primary artifact is, how runs are triggered, how Instagram Reels are accessed, and what happens when every remote provider fails.

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] **D16 — Obsidian vault is the delivery surface (OQ-2).** The canonical store stays the project directory (JSON, per ADR-004 D2). A **projection step** writes human-facing Markdown into an Obsidian vault:

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] ```text ~/Obsidian/knowledge-vault/ Sources/ # one note per source, frontmatter + timestamped claims Notes/ # per-source distilled notes Knowledge/ # atomic knowledge units as notes, [[wikilinks]] between them Procedures/ # step-by-step procedures Content/ # publishable drafts Attachments/ # audio/frames only if retention allows (OQ-8) Templates/ # source.md, knowledge.md, procedure.md, content.md ```

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] Rules: - JSON is canonical; Markdown is generated and **never hand-edited as source of truth** (a hand-edit is detected by hash and reported, not silently overwritten). - Every projected note carries frontmatter: `source_id`, `source_uri`, `provider`, `model`, `generated_at`, `schema_version`, `content_hash`. - Wikilinks use knowledge-unit ids (`[[k-1a2b3c4d5e6f]]`), so the vault graph mirrors the knowledge graph. - Obsidian is a *viewer*: no plugin is required for correctness. Dataview is optional.

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] **D17 — Publishable content is the primary output (OQ-4).** Notes, knowledge units and procedures are **intermediate** artifacts whose purpose is to support publishable drafts in `Content/`. Consequences: - Content drafts must cite the knowledge units they use, and those units must cite sources + timestamps (keeps AC-06/AC-15 meaningful end-to-end). - A draft with no resolvable unit citations fails verification. - FR-18 (original content separation) becomes a `Must` for release, not a `Should`.
[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] **D18 — Daemon trigger (OQ-7).** A `systemd --user` service (`kas-daemon`) watches an inbox and runs the pipeline:

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] ```text ~/ai-agent-ecosystem/runtime/inbox/ # drop a job file (yaml) here ~/ai-agent-ecosystem/runtime/queue/ # claimed jobs ~/ai-agent-ecosystem/runtime/done/ # completed, with evidence pointer ~/ai-agent-ecosystem/runtime/failed/ # escalated, with diagnostics ```

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] - One worker at a time per project (lockfile), jobs processed FIFO. - CLI remains available (`kas run --project <dir>`) for one-shot work and tests. - The daemon is a thin shell around the same orchestrator; no logic lives only in it.

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] **D19 — Reels access requires cookies (OQ-9).** Instagram/Facebook Reels need an authenticated session. Plan: - Preferred: `yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser firefox` (Firefox profile exists on the host), so no credential file is written by us. - Fallback: an exported Netscape `cookies.txt` at `~/.hermes/cookies/instagram.txt`, mode `600`, referenced by path in config — never copied into the repo or artifacts. - Public-only mode is the default when cookies are absent: login-gated reels are `quarantined` with a named reason, not silently skipped. - Cookies expire. The daemon must detect auth failur...

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] **D20 — No local fallback (OQ-10).** There is no local model runtime on the host, so D8's offline mode cannot cover extraction. If LLM7 and Unorouter both fail beyond the retry budget, the job is marked `failed` with `escalated: true` and the run stops. No degraded output is produced. Ingestion, checksumming and transcript storage still work offline.

[docs/decisions/ADR-006-output-trigger-sources.md] ## Consequences - A markdown projection layer and its tests are added to Phase 2 scope. - Obsidian must be installed on the host (flatpak, user scope, no root needed). - The daemon is Phase 5 work, but its directories and locking rules are fixed now. - Because content is the primary output, OQ-6 (copyright/consent) becomes urgent: publishable drafts over copyrighted reels must synthesise, not reproduce, source text. - Cookie handling becomes a documented operational task with an expiry failure mode.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] # ADR-004 — Phase 0 requirements freeze - **Date:** 2026-11-02 - **Status:** Accepted (pending Director sign-off on blocking open questions) - **Deciders:** Director, Orchestrator - **Supersedes:** none - **Related:** requirements v2.0, acceptance-criteria v1.0, open-questions v1.0

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] ## Context The project shipped as a documentation scaffold (v1.0): structure, contracts and prompts existed, but no requirement was testable and no artifact contract was defined. Phase 0 of the implementation plan requires frozen requirements, a Director's Section and acceptance criteria before any code is written.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D1 — Adapter-based source model.** Every origin is normalized into one Source Record (requirements §4). Adapters are pluggable and may not change the record. *Consequence:* new origins are additive; the core pipeline never branches on source kind.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D2 — Fixed artifact layout.** The project-root directory contract in requirements §6 is frozen. *Consequence:* tests and agents can assert paths; no agent may invent directories.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D3 — Content-addressed identifiers.** `source_id = src-<sha256[0:12]>`, `knowledge unit id = k-<sha256(statement)[0:12]>`. *Consequence:* determinism and idempotency (AC-12, AC-13) fall out of the design instead of being bolted on.
[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D4 — Raw sources are immutable.** A checksum conflict is a hard failure, never an overwrite. *Consequence:* provenance is trustworthy; re-ingest is safe.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D5 — Verification is a gate, not a report.** Completion without an `evidence/<task_id>.json` with `result: "pass"` is rejected by the orchestrator (AC-10). *Consequence:* "done" is falsifiable.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D6 — Fail-fast configuration.** Unknown manifest or config keys are errors (AC-19). *Consequence:* typos surface immediately instead of producing silently degraded runs.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D7 — Bounded retries with escalation.** `max_retries` (default 3) then stop the branch and record `escalated: true` (AC-11). *Consequence:* no infinite loops, no hidden repeated failures.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D8 — Offline-first, network opt-in.** `network.enabled: false` is the default; egress attempts are blocked and logged (AC-16, AC-17). *Consequence:* reproducible and privacy-preserving by default.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D9 — Phase gates are exit tests.** Phase transitions require the named criteria to pass (acceptance-criteria §4), not a verbal claim. *Consequence:* the roadmap becomes mechanically checkable.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] **D10 — Unanswered questions are recorded, not guessed.** Blocking questions live in `open-questions.md` with an explicit default used only if the Director waives them. *Consequence:* satisfies the Director's "do not silently invent missing inputs" non-negotiable.

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] ## Consequences - Phase 1 can start on manifest/config/status without resolving OQ-1…OQ-4, but **Phase 2 cannot**. - Every later behaviour change requires a new ADR and a version bump (requirements §10). - The `VERSION` field in the packaged Skill must track the requirements version (AC-22).

[docs/decisions/ADR-004-phase0-freeze.md] ## Open items OQ-1 (source kinds), OQ-2 (output destination), OQ-3 (model runtime), OQ-4 (knowledge definition), OQ-7 (trigger) are blocking for their phase. OQ-5, OQ-6, OQ-8 have safe defaults.
